name: Moldova

chips.label: Band 2: Durable
chips.why: MI v3.3 score band based on five equally weighted pillars.
chips.rule: The MI score is grouped into five public score bands.

chips.label: Earned prosperity
chips.why: Institutions roughly match or exceed the level predicted by income, which suggests greater durability.
chips.rule: MI residual vs. the log-GDP regression (the durability gap): below -0.03 → granted, otherwise earned (a ±0.03 tolerance treats near-zero gaps as in-line).

chips.label: Lopsided · weakest: Economic Complexity
chips.why: The gap between the strongest and weakest pillar shows how balanced the country's structure is.

verdict: Structurally durable, prosperity roughly in line with institutions, lopsided (economic complexity the weak point).

checks.title: Durability gate
checks.headline: earned-vs-granted +0.01
checks.detail: Prosperity sits roughly in line with institutions. No durability warning here.

checks.title: Weakest link
checks.headline: Economic Complexity is lowest
checks.detail: Economic Complexity is the lowest pillar and the main source of imbalance in the score.

checks.title: Room to rise
checks.headline: already high
checks.detail: The institutional starting level is already high, and large further increases are uncommon in the historical data.

safeguards.name: Durability Gate (P4-P1 gap)
safeguards.headline: income-institutions gap +0.30 · flagged
safeguards.detail: Economic Structure-Institutions gap = 0.296 >= 0.28 (crisis floor): income/economy has outrun institutions (granted/fragile), structurally vulnerable under stress.
safeguards.modification: Flag elevated structural crisis-vulnerability; pair with stability (P5)/shock exposure. Risk, not timing (Mod8).
safeguards.why: Independently derived on 21 crisis/absorber cases: the level gap between income (P4) and institutions (P1) separated real crises from shock-absorbers at 83% sensitivity / 100% specificity. When income has outrun institutions, the state is structurally crisis-prone under shock: 'granted/fragile'.

safeguards.name: Rentier Capture (Bidirectional)
safeguards.headline: below 15% of GDP · no penalty
safeguards.detail: Resource rents 0.2% of GDP: below 15% (no penalty).
safeguards.why: Resource income can distort measures of institutional strength or help governments maintain elite support. This check marks rents above 15 percent of GDP and treats levels above 25 percent as severe.

safeguards.name: External Administration
safeguards.headline: no such condition
safeguards.why: Under the Dayton OHR, Bosnia's WGI scores partly reflected the external administrator's capacity. This safeguard discounts P1 when an external administration is doing much of the governing.

safeguards.name: Capacity Gate
safeguards.headline: no such condition
safeguards.detail: Institutions = 0.519, successors = N/A. Gate not triggered.
safeguards.why: Sudan produced only two successor states, but the outcome was still the worst in the sample because institutional capacity was very low. A small number of fragments is not reassuring when P1 is that weak.

safeguards.name: Reversal Risk
safeguards.headline: no such condition
safeguards.why: The framework captured Tunisia's initial improvement but missed the 2021 presidential self-coup. This safeguard marks democratic transitions with weak economic results as vulnerable to reversal.

safeguards.name: Predatory Neighbor / Exogenous Shock
safeguards.headline: condition present
safeguards.detail: Neighbor threat: high. Russian pressure; Russian troops/Transnistria breakaway region. Institutions provides some resilience. Framework diagnoses vulnerability to shock, not the shock itself.
safeguards.modification: Note endogenous prediction separately. Flag that outcome may be externally imposed rather than internally generated.
safeguards.why: External threats can overwhelm a country even when its internal structure is sound. This safeguard records those threats separately from conditions inside the country.

safeguards.name: Sub-State Turbulence
safeguards.headline: no such condition
safeguards.why: A state can remain intact while dealing with repeated government collapses, high anti-system voting, or sharp regional divisions. This check measures that ongoing burden, not the likelihood of collapse.

safeguards.name: Suppression vs Prevention
safeguards.headline: no such condition
safeguards.why: This safeguard separates military suppression, legal or institutional de-escalation, and power-sharing. In the case studies, renewed suppression after a period of power-sharing had the worst outcomes.

safeguards.name: Porosity-with-Backstop
safeguards.headline: no such condition
safeguards.why: This safeguard tests whether support from a major outside power makes renewed suppression and partial reunification more likely than permanent independence.

strategy.explanation: P1 = 0.519. Insufficient context signals to classify strategy. Could be transitioning between strategies or running a hybrid.

structural_vulnerability.reading: Income and economic development have moved ahead of institutional strength. The historical cases associate this gap with higher risk under stress.

vulnerability.summary: Risk level: LOW. P1 = 0.519, spread = 0.401, 2 safeguards active.

accountability_gap.reading: Accountability is broadly in line with state capacity and income.
accountability_gap.caveat: Exploratory note (v3.2): informational; orthogonal to the durability gap; no crisis validation yet.
